portion_doctrine: Segments 31-40 of series_5_download.docx are transcribed SEO/AI marketing masterclasses: (1) Surfer Academy on topical authority + AI content creation (ch 1-7); (2) Boring Marketer on leveraging Claude Code for local SEO (ch 1-7, 6 hours to 4-figure-per-day ROI); (3) Neil Patel on AI SEO metrics (5 signals for tracking AI citations, brand search lift, predictive traffic, GEO metrics, conversion lift); (4) Local SEO complete system (Google Business Profile optimization, Core 30 page structure, relevance vs authority, local rank maps). REAL content: 85% substantive tactics, 15% boilerplate/ads. Gold: topical authority decision tree, Core 30 architecture, AI citation tracking, Boring Marketer tech stack setup.
operating_rules: Topical authority beats random keywords: build clusters by search intent, not volume. Money pages first, then support clusters one per funnel.
4-phase content creation: research (top 5 competitors), structure (outline matching intent), write (AI + human expertise), optimize (against Surfer score 0-100).

Content moat via original assets: data, case studies, interviews, proprietary knowledge. AI slop baseline is 96% of web getting zero traffic; differentiate via human layer (screenshots, workflow detail, real outcomes).

On-page SEO checklist: title tag (keyword front-loaded, under 60 chars), H1 (mirrors title), H2/H3 hierarchy, URL (short + keyword), meta description (150-160 chars, action-oriented), internal links (context-aware, not footer), image optimization (descriptive filenames + alt text).

Link building tactic pyramid: Tier 1 (be the source: original data journalists cite), Tier 2 (HARO/journalist queries 15 min/day, 100 queries for 1 link), Tier 3 (linkable assets: calculators, templates, comprehensive guides).

Local SEO three-glass model: Proximity (unchangeable), Relevance (build via content), Authority (build via links). Most locals are 50% full on relevance/authority; 10-15 pieces to rank in weeks not months.

Core 30 architecture: 1 homepage + 3-4 category pages + 25-30 service pages. Homepage has 8 consistency signals (title, H1, Maps embed, secondary categories in H2s, review widget, address match, phone match, schema). Internal links flow homepage → categories → services (editorial links only, not footer).

Google Business Profile audit: 10 categories minimum (not 1), 20-30 services minimum, fill every box (750 char description, 20+ photos, posts, attributes). 30 minutes of work puts you ahead of 90% of locals.

Local rank map decision tree: If top-3% below threshold (25-50% of competitor leader), build topical relevance (supporting content, FAQ answers). If at/above threshold, shift to geographical content (neighborhood pages, location-service combos).

Technical optimization quick wins: Google Page Speed Insights (free, copy/paste errors to Claude Code), robots.txt, XML sitemap, image compression (webp format), alt text refresh, redirect chains, broken links. Screaming Frog SEO Spider crawls 500 URLs free.

AI SEO signals: brand search surge (up 25-50% when LLM recommends), AI citations (check weekly via Surfer AI Tracker across ChatGPT/Gemini/Perplexity), conversion lift from AI traffic (9% vs 3% from organic = 3x better). Content older than 18 months without refresh shows declining citation rate.

Development environment for non-technical: install Claude Code (terminal command), link GitHub repo (version control), deploy via Vercel (auto-update on GitHub push). Anima plugin converts Figma designs to React components Claude can assemble.

Keyword research simplified (vibe marketing): ask Claude 'give me 25-50 keywords I should optimize around' without overthinking volume/competition. Analyze for search intent (emergency vs information vs service-ready). Find keywords where searcher is ready to act (call button, credit card).

SEO audit prompt: Use ultra think mode (Opus), ask Claude to 'go through this website in extreme detail, find all technical and on-page SEO issues, then fix them.' It will discover missing files, slow load times, schema markup gaps, then execute fixes.

Sub-agents tactic: spin up 3+ parallel agents in Claude Code (one for missing alt text, one for competitor analysis, one for other fixes) while continuing main work. Agents surface opportunities in background.

30-day quick-start plan: Week 1 (GSC setup, keyword research, intent analysis, identify money pages); Week 2 (write/optimize 1 money page, full on-page checklist); Week 3 (publish 1 mid-funnel piece linked to money page + related content); Week 4 (HARO queries 15 min/day, check AI visibility, monitor GSC for early signals).

AI visibility tracking non-negotiable: use Surfer AI Tracker or manual test (incognito ChatGPT, ask core topic question). Top brands get cited 20-30% of relevant queries, average 5-12%, below 3% = invisible. Rankings and AI citations are two separate scores.

Local merchant links tier 2: Chamber of Commerce ($200-300/year, join multiple if within 70 mi), sponsorships of youth sports/charities/community events. Each link signals local trust to Google and AI systems. Not AI slop links; medium-quality external validation.

Content structure for local service pages: title tag (service + city), H1 (matches title), body targets specific service details, NOT generic 5-ways advice. Write about this service in this city with this business's nuances. AI writes baseline, human editor adds photos, callouts, formatting, personality.

FAQ generation discipline: reword 'people also ask' questions (don't copy verbatim). Use different word order to avoid abuse-pattern detection. Each FAQ page is supporting content, linked back to core service page. Google sees these as expertise signals.
prompts: Give me a list of 25-50 keywords that relate to [my website / my service / my business]. I don't need volume or competition metrics, just keywords that make sense for my business.

Go through this website [URL/codebase] in extreme detail using ultra think. Spend extra time finding all the technical and on-page SEO issues and opportunities we can fix together so I can dominate the local market. List everything, then fix them.
Launch three agents. One to find all missing alt text or pages under 300 words. One to analyze my top 5 competitors. One to identify all other technical fixes I should be doing on my website.

You are an expert SEO content writer. For [target keyword], write content that: targets the exact search intent, covers the topics competitors missed, matches the average depth (3000+ words if top results are long), includes original data/case studies/customer quotes/screenshots, and maintains topical authority. Structure with H2/H3 hierarchy. Target Surfer AI score above [threshold]. Avoid AI slop via specific details, real outcomes, and voice.

Using GMBB Everywhere and this category list [paste categories], help me choose 2-4 strategic Google Business Profile categories beyond my primary, looking at related categories competitors selected and search volume.
Generate 20-30 Google Business Profile services for a [business type] with these categories [paste categories]. Services should be semantically relevant to each category. Format: one per line.

Generate 52 unique Google Business Profile posts (one per week) for a [business type] that: includes promotions, educational tips, local community mentions, seasonal updates, service highlights. Make them conversational, 60-80 words each. Format as numbered list.

Find local sponsorship and link-building opportunities in [city/area]. Return: name of organization, type (chamber/charity/sports league), typical cost range, URL, link value, contact info. Format as a table.

gates: Core 30 architecture must match GBP categories/services exactly before publishing. No orphan pages.
Never publish topical content until rank map run shows below-threshold top-3%. Otherwise waste of content.
Internal links must be editorial (in-paragraph, context-aware), not footer/navigation. Navigation links barely pass authority.
All consistency signals must align homepage-to-GBP character-for-character: address, phone, title, H1, schema.
At least 20 external links (non-AI-slop) required per core 30 before expecting competitive ranking. Without links, Google can't verify AI content is trustworthy.

Every page on a local site must serve GBP ranking goal. Generic blog posts (5 ways to X, history of plumbing) do not rank in local. Only answer specific local questions or risk wasting content budget.
Freshness signal: content older than 18 months without updates shows declining AI citation rates. Establish quarterly refresh calendar before launch.
AI visibility tracking required monthly. If brands not appearing in ChatGPT/Perplexity for core topics, topical authority or consistency signals failing. Audit and fix.
Ranking #1 Google gives only 31% chance of AI citation. Separate strategy required for AI search. Content depth + clarity + citations from other authority sites = AI visibility.
Homepage landing page must have 8 consistency signals. Missing even 1 signals to Google that website and GBP are unrelated or untrustworthy.

Service pages must be location + service specific, not generic. 'Water heater replacement Houston' content must differ from 'water heater replacement Dallas.' Same service, different city = different FAQ, different service costs, different local context.
Mobile version must be fast (load in snap, high Page Speed score) or rank lower. AI content + slow site = negative signal.
contradictions: Google ranks both organic URLs and GBP. Local rank maps measure GBP only. This doc emphasizes 60-70% of clicks go to top 3 map positions, suggesting website SEO is secondary. But later sections recommend full website architecture + internal linking as if website ranking matters equally. Clarification: website matters for building topical authority signaling to Google that GBP is legitimate; website traffic is bonus.

Boring Marketer built a 4-hour website that ranked in days. Local SEO complete system says 'you probably won't see results in 30 days.' Tension between immediate-impact setup and realistic ranking timelines. Boring Marketer had minimal competition and light keyword difficulty; the local plumber doc is designed for more competitive markets (Houston vs Charlotte).

AI content baseline is 96% of web getting zero traffic (Surfer), but this doc advocates extensive AI use for local site generation. Contradiction resolved: AI content fails when generic and alone. AI content succeeds when: (1) paired with original data/voice/screenshots, (2) built on topical authority foundation, (3) validated by external links, (4) optimized for AI citation via consistency signals.

Topical vs geographical content decision tree: doc says if below threshold, build topical (FAQ/supporting pages). But also says blog posts don't work locally. Clarification: topical supporting content = FAQ answers and service-detail pages that answer specific local questions, NOT generic SEO blog posts. The difference is specificity and internal linking to money pages.
content_ideas: Location page template: [city] + [primary service], include landmarks specific to city, common issues in that city's climate/infrastructure, local case studies or local sports references, FAQs about service in that area, link to service page and homepage category.

Service page depth template: what it is, why customers need it, what it includes, how long it takes, what to expect, cost range, comparison to DIY, when to call emergency, maintenance tips, real before/after photos, customer testimonials, FAQ reworded from people-also-ask.

Homepage consistency template: 8 signals in order: title tag (primary category + city + brand), H1 matching title, Google Maps embed, secondary category H2s (50-100 words each with editorial link to category page), review widget, address (character-match GBP), phone (character-match GBP), local business schema.

GBP automation template: (1) weekly posts via prompt (52-post year generator), (2) weekly geotagged photos (smartphone auto-geotags), (3) AI review responses (25 seconds setup), (4) automated citations (Apple Maps, Bing, Yelp, etc.).

AI citation improvement playbook: (1) audit current citations via Surfer AI Tracker (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini), (2) identify gaps (competitors cited, you're not), (3) refresh content older than 18 months, (4) add FAQ schema + clear H2/H3 structure, (5) earn more external links (chamber, sponsorships), (6) monitor weekly.

Boring Marketer SOP for non-technical founders: (1) ask Claude Code for keyword list, (2) request SEO audit with ultra-think, (3) spin up 3 sub-agents for parallel tasks, (4) ask Claude to build website in Figma + convert via Anima, (5) deploy via GitHub → Vercel, (6) get organic leads within 24 hours.

Local SEO competitive analysis deck: run rank maps for top 3 competitors for your primary keyword, identify their top-3% coverage, determine if market is 'Gary, Indiana' (90% achievable) vs 'Houston' (25-30% realistic), set 30-day goal at 25-50% of leader's top-3%.

The NOT-AI-slop link strategy: for each of 30 core pages, find 1+ external links from reasonable domains (not directory spam, not PBN). Sources: relevant blogs in your niche, local news, industry publications, sponsorship directories, chamber listings. Cost: $35/link via Ice Cream Truck or DIY outreach.

Seasonal content refresh calendar: Q1 (update water heater/heating content), Q2 (AC/cooling), Q3 (inspections before winter), Q4 (holiday promotions + emergency prep). Sheet: [date, page, update type, owner].
weird_gold: The Glass Metaphor works for Google AND AI: the three glasses (proximity, relevance, authority) that Google uses to rank GBP are the exact same signals ChatGPT and LLMs use to recommend brands. Consistency signals = both Google AND AI trust = customer finds you in map AND gets recommended by ChatGPT = 2x authority.

Navigator links barely pass authority, but editorial links in body copy pass real authority. Google distinguishes. This means footer/mega-menu links (navigation) are structure, not endorsement. Only in-paragraph links count as 'this page vouches for that page.'

Boring Marketer earned $1000s in 24 hours on a local mechanic site built in 4 hours via Claude Code. The founder had zero coding experience. This proves the moat is NOT code skill anymore; it's knowing the right questions to ask. (Vertical expertise, not code craft.)

Neil Patel data: 75% of AI citations go to sources that DON'T rank in Google top 10. Rankings and AI citations are completely uncorrelated now. You can rank #1 and be invisible to AI; you can rank page 3 and be cited constantly by LLMs. The game changed.

GPT 5.3 to 5.4 model upgrade: branded citations jumped from 8% to 56% (7x lift in one release). Model versions matter. Tracking AI citations weekly is non-negotiable because the numbers change dramatically with model releases.

Topical authority threshold is 25-50% of the leader's top-3%. So if your market leader achieves 80% top-3% coverage, your threshold for 'Google trusts you as an expert' is just 20-40% top-3%. You don't need to match them; you just need to prove you know what you're doing.

Boring Marketer's sub-agents hack: spin up 3+ parallel agents while working in main thread. Main agent (you) keeps building. Sub-agents surface opportunities in background. This is distributed thinking at protocol level; not about hiring team, about Claude Code orchestration.

The people-also-ask abuse pattern: Google knows SEOs copy these questions verbatim. So if you copy exactly, Google's transformer model flags 'this looks like template abuse.' Rephrase slightly (different word order, same meaning) to avoid penalty. Transformer tech (same as ChatGPT) can evaluate semantic meaning, not just word order.

No blog posts. Only supporting content with PURPOSE. Every page = answer a specific local question nobody is ranking for, AND link back to money pages. The difference between 'write a blog post' and 'answer a gap in local search' is 90% of why local agencies fail.

30 pages of average content beats 3 pages of great content in local SEO. The Core 30 strategy works because 30 pages of topical relevance (even with AI + light human edit) signals to Google 'this business actually does all these things.' Depth of site structure matters more than polish in competitive markets.
